q: Past practical exam (2011–2012 sets): answer the questions on the slide.
a:
What makes structures white: (a) CT – calcium (renal stone); (b) MRI T2 – fluid (CSF)

CT: whiteness = high attenuation (high HU: calcium, bone, contrast, fresh blood). MRI T2: water/CSF is hyperintense (white). The same "white" means different physics in each technique.

q: Past practical exam (2011–2012 sets): answer the questions on the slide.
a:
(a) CT – calcification (renal stone); (b) CT brain – acute haemorrhage

Both are hyperdense on CT: calcium (> 200 HU) and fresh clotted blood (50–90 HU).
